 Order

The present contempt petition is filed by the complainant against the accused to take action on the accused under the provisions of 11 and 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, for willful disobedience of the order dated 17th September, 2019 made in Writ Petitions No.27392 and 30320 of 2019 wherein the learned Single Judge, while disposing of the writ petition, directed the respondents to consider the grievance of the petitioners and pass a speaking order and communicate the decision to each of the petitioners within a period of four months from the date of receipt of certified copy of the order.
Since the order of the learned Single Judge has not been complied with by the accused deliberately, the complainant was forced to file the present contempt petition on 08th July, 2020.
This Court issued notice to the accused.

In response to the notice issued to the accused, Mr. Ajith M, working as Special Land Acquisition Officer, Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board (METRO), filed the compliance affidavit dated 17th March, 2023.

At paragraphs 4 to 6 of the Affidavit, it is stated as under:
B Shantilal vs Vijay Kumar on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129687097/
2

"I submit that, this Hon'ble Court was pleased to direct the concerned respondent in the WP to examine the grievance of the petitioners ad pass the speaking order etc.,
whether petitioners are entitled to redress his grievance or not within a period of 4 months from the date of receipt of the copy of the order.

I took charge as Special LAO, KIADB (METRO), Bengaluru on - 06.12.2021, i.e. subsequent to passing of the order dated 17.09.2019.
5.
I submit that, after receipt of the notice in the above case, I have called concerned officials and instructed put up the file and noted the following facts from the records.
After receipt of the representation, the then Spl. LAO has addressed a letter on 25.10.2019 to the BMRCL to examine the same as per Annexure-F.

The complainants have receive the compensation on 05.07.2018 and 29.12.2018 by entering into agreement under Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act by way of consent in full and final settlement in lieu of acquisition of the land coupled with indemnity Bond.
The amounts were transferred to their respective Bank accounts by means of RTGS.

The copies of the agreements executed by the complainants under Section 29(2) of the Act and the payment receipts are herewith produced and marked as Annexures R1 and R2.
6.
I submit that, the grievance of the petitioners was that the are entitled for compensation amount than what was paid under Section 29(2) of the Act.
I have examined the said grievance of the petitioners and perused the available material and considered the grievance of the petitioners.

As per law the petitioners are not entitled for any more amount, once when the compensation was paid by agreement/consent under Section 29(2) of the Act as such the claim of the complainants was rejected and suitable endorsement dated 14.03.2023 was issued to the complainants.
The same has been sent to the complainants address by RP&AD.
The copy of the endorsement dated 14.3.2023 is herewith produced and marked as Annexure-R3.

Thus the order of the Hon'ble Court at Annexure-E has been duly complied with."
2.

The order passed by the learned Single Judge on 17th September, 2019 directing the accused to consider the representations made by the petitioners within a period of four months from the date of receipt of certified copy of the order, and the accused ought to have passed the order on or before 01st January, 2020, but the accused has not passed any orders and unnecessarily driven the complainant before this Court by filing the present contempt petition on 08 th July, 2020.
Even after contempt petition is filed, the accused has not bothered.
When this Court issued notice on 09 th February, 2023, the present affidavit is filed.

There is a delay of more than two and a half years in complying with the order passed by the learned Single Judge and thereby the complainant is unnecessarily driven to this Court in the present contempt petition by engaging Lawyer and spending litigation expenses, so also, undergone mental trauma.
At last, the accused, has now passed the order on 14 th March, 2023, and complied with the order passed by the learned Single Judge.
Since the order of compliance is passed after a delay of two and half years, this contempt petition has to be disposed of by imposing cost.

In view of the above, we pass the following:

3 ORDER i) Contempt proceedings are hereby dropped, subject to accused paying the cost of Rs.25,000/- to each of the complainants within a period of two weeks;
ii) It is needless to observe it is always open for complainants to challenge the endorsement dated 14th March, 2023 if so desired, in accordance with law.
